messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × the radius of Jupiter** (about 180,000 km). Its mass is estimated to be around **10 × the mass of Jupiter**, placing it at the upper end of the planetary mass range—just below the deuterium‑burning limit that separates planets from brown dwarfs.  

Because exoplanet discoveries are continually being refined, future observations may reveal even larger bodies, but as of now HD 100546 b holds the record for the largest confirmed exoplanet.
